title: #herethereareblueberries #newyorktheatreworkshop #nytw #tectonictheat...
transcript: Last night, I saw Here There Are Blueberries at New York Theatre Workshop, a co-production with Tectonic Theater Project. This play is about an album of photos from a concentration camp during the Holocaust and follows the investigative work done by the US Holocaust Memorial Museum to identify who was in them, and what they could reveal about this piece of history. The text is largely excerpts from interviews and other primary sources, and as an audience member, we’re really along for the ride in how this album was investigated in what was discovered. The photographs are almost like their own character in the play as they’re integral to the storytelling and the visual vocabulary of this piece. I thought the ways that the actors interacted with the projections was really cool and theatrical. And overall I felt like this was a very dark and moving piece, and if you like documentary theater I think you will really enjoy it. But even if not, what this piece posits about human psychology in response to the horrors carried out by the subjects of these images I think is quite interesting. With that, another program for my collection.
